data.name: Sample - Microsoft 365 Defender - 1.2.1
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Microsoft 365 Defender" connector. If you are planning to use the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Triage Defender Incident to Response
workflows.description:
The flagship loop for the M365 trial: fetch Active Microsoft 365 Defender incidents oldest-first, pull the oldest one in full, hunt its devices in Advanced Hunting for last-24h network activity, create a FortiSOAR alert that records the triage, then ask a human through a Microsoft Teams approval card. Approve and the playbook updates the Defender incident (status In Progress, classification TruePositive) and runs the Graph-side containment - the reported source IP is appended to a Conditional Access IP named location and the compromised user's sessions are revoked. Reject and the incident is left open with an explanatory comment on the matching Graph security alert; nothing is changed on either surface.
Why oldest-first: Defender's incident list answers newest-first, and a backlog demo wants the STALEST unhandled incident, so the playbook sorts the fetched list by createdTime itself instead of relying on API order.
Why a SOAR alert mid-playbook: the Defender incident is the detection, the FortiSOAR alert is the case - the approval card links to it, and the update comment names it, so the response trail starts and ends on records a SOC actually works.
Inputs: approver (Teams recipient for the approval card - default soc-oncall@contoso.example), reported_ip (the source IP to block - default 198.51.100.7), named_location_id (the existing IP named location the IP is appended to; the op appends, it does not create - default is the sample location id), graph_alert_id (the Graph security alerts_v2 id the reject-branch comment goes on; Graph alert ids are a different surface from Defender alertIds, so the caller supplies the Graph-side id - default is the sample alert id). Outputs: outcome (responded, held or nothing_to_triage), incident_id, soar_alert, compromised_user, revoked, named_location.
Live prerequisites: the Defender connector configured against a tenant with the M365 Defender plane licensed, the microsoft-graph_dev connector configured (User.RevokeSessions.All, Policy.Read.All, SecurityAlert.Read. .. for the comment), and an existing IP named location for the block. The advanced_hunting query is read-only KQL over DeviceNetworkEvents.

arguments.device_count: {{ ((vars.steps.Get_Incident.data.alerts | default([], true)) | map(attribute='entities') | map('default', [], true) | sum(start=[]) | selectattr('entityType', 'equalto', 'Device') | map(attribute='deviceName') | unique | list) | length }}

params.Query:
DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(24h) and DeviceName in (dynamic({{ vars.device_list_json }})) | summarize EventCount=count(), BytesSent=sum(RemoteSize), IsExternal=any(IsExternal)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName

Compromised user: {{ vars.compromised_user }}. Devices in evidence: {{ vars.device_count }}. {% if vars.steps.Device_Hunt.data is defined %}Advanced Hunting matched {{ ((vars.steps.Device_Hunt.data | default({}, true)).Results | default([], true)) | length }} network-activity row(s) in the last 24h.{% else %}Advanced Hunting did not return data for this run (the query failed; see the run log).{% endif %} Response pending approval.

arguments.name: Microsoft Graph API (fork)

groups.name: Note: List Incidents
groups.description: Active incidents only, all pages (get_all_records). The datetime params are left off on purpose: they must carry fractional seconds or the connector refuses the run before any HTTP call, and a triage sweep wants everything Active, not a time slice.

groups.name: Note: Extract Context
groups.description: The incident's evidence carries the hunt targets: device names feed the Advanced Hunting query, the user entities name the accounts whose sessions get revoked on approval. Entities flatten across alerts; a null entities list (fresh incidents) collapses to nothing through the default filters instead of failing the render.

groups.name: Note: Device Hunt
groups.description: Read-only KQL over DeviceNetworkEvents for the incident's devices in the last 24h - the "what did these machines actually do" slice a responder wants before approving containment. The device list is injected as a KQL dynamic() array built from the incident evidence.

groups.name: Note: Update Incident
groups.description: Status and classification carry the decision; the comment names the SOAR alert so the Defender incident points back at the case record. Values are the connector's own display keys ('In Progress' maps to the API's InProgress on the wire).

groups.name: Note: Block IPs
groups.description: The Conditional Access half of the containment, on Graph: the reported IP is appended to an existing IP named location (existing ranges are preserved). The named location must exist - create it once per tenant and pass its id; block_new_ips refuses trusted locations and non-IP locations by design.

groups.name: Note: Revoke Sessions
groups.description: revokeSignInSessions kills every token issued so far for the compromised account - the user re-authenticates, an attacker holding a stolen session cookie is out.

groups.name: Note: Reject Comment
groups.description: Graph security alerts_v2 ids are a different surface from Defender alertIds, so the caller passes the Graph-side alert to annotate (graph_alert_id); on a live tenant that id comes from the matching alert in the Graph security API.

groups.name: Note: Nothing To Triage
groups.description: A clean no-op: no Active incidents (or the fetch answered empty). Scheduled runs land here most days, which is the point.
